transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2027-04-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (Bluebridge Procurement), Anil Rao (Bluebridge InfoSec), Marcus Liu (Bluebridge Finance), Priya Shah (Bluebridge Legal)

Summary:
Quick intake workshop focused on procurement path for a pilot: clarify MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations for Dedicated vs Hosted, KMS/SSO requirements, and pricing approval thresholds. Action items and next steps captured at end.

Topics:
- MSA redlines and DPA data residency
- SLA uptime & breach remedies for Dedicated (reserved) vs Hosted
- Key management (customer-managed KMS) and encryption at rest
- SSO (SAML) integration and least-privilege RBAC
- Pricing bands, committed spend, pilot SOW

Transcript:
00:00:00 Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Uh, I think we have forty five minutes ish, quick workshop to align on the procurement and legal asks. Samir from my side will cover the technical bits for Dedicated and KMS.
00:00:18 Samir Patel (Redwood SE): Hi all. Quick note: I might say 'KV cache' and someone transcribed it as 'K V catch' in the last call, so heads up if I mis-say some jargon.
00:00:26 Laura Kim (Bluebridge Procurement): Thanks, Maya. We're trying to get the pilot greenlit this quarter. Procurement needs to understand the MSA/DPA redlines and any pricing thresholds that require board approval. Marcus is here for budget sign-off questions.
00:00:40 Marcus Liu (Bluebridge Finance): Yep, budget is sensitive. We need a clear committed spend number and default auto-renew triggers. Also approval path — if it's over $250k annually it hits the finance committee.
00:00:52 Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Understood. Quick preface: Redwood offers Hosted API for easiest start, Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and Private deployments for heavy compliance. For the pilot we usually recommend Dedicated small pool so you get reliable performance while not requiring full private on-prem.
00:01:12 Priya Shah (Bluebridge Legal): We're reviewing the MSA/DPA. Two initial asks: 1) stricter data deletion commitments and 2) audit rights — we want SOC 2 type 2 report and ability to review subprocessor list quarterly.
00:01:28 Samir Patel (Redwood SE): For the KMS question — we support customer-managed KMS via provider-managed HSMs, and we can bring keys into a VPC/private deployment for full key isolation. For Dedicated we offer envelope encryption with your KMS; that does mean some additional latency — usually in the low single-digit milliseconds, but we'll share bench numbers.
00:01:58 Anil Rao (Bluebridge InfoSec): Latency is less of a concern for batch jobs but for our front-line credit decisioning low-latency matters. Also data residency — we need logs and any cached KV objects kept in-region (EU-West) and not replicated to US without consent.
00:02:14 Maya Chen (Redwood AE): That's a great point. We can pin region routing in the deployment config and apply a no-cross-region policy for the account. We'll put that in the DPA appendix.
00:02:26 Marcus Liu (Bluebridge Finance): On pricing, can you share a committed tier pricing table and also the pricing for burst / overage? We need to model a scenario where we double token usage in month three.
00:02:40 Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Absolutely. We'll send the Dedicated pricing spreadsheet — the pilot SOW will include an agreed committed token/throughput level, burst caps, and a rate card for overage. For overage we typically have tiered discounts depending on commit.
00:02:55 Laura Kim (Bluebridge Procurement): What's the approval timeline for any MSA exceptions? Our legal needs to know how quickly Redwood can respond to redlines.
00:03:04 Maya Chen (Redwood AE): From our experience, simple redlines we can turn around 3-5 business days; if there are nonstandard security clauses or data residency changes it could be 7-14 business days. We'll aim for the shorter end for the pilot.
00:03:17 Priya Shah (Bluebridge Legal): Can you confirm liability caps? Our standard is three months' fees for SaaS — is Redwood flexible here?
00:03:26 Maya Chen (Redwood AE): We typically negotiate liability caps with enterprise customers; for pilots we can offer a limited deviation but would need that to be scoped in the commercial terms. I'll flag that as a negotiation point with legal.
00:03:38 Samir Patel (Redwood SE): On the technical side, two notes: 1) KV cache and prefix caching are in-memory on the Dedicated nodes; if you require no persistence at all we can set retention to zero and disable any disk spill. 2) For SSO we support SAML and OIDC and can map groups to RBAC roles in the console.
00:03:59 Anil Rao (Bluebridge InfoSec): Good — for RBAC we need role separation between dev/test and production and audit trails. How long do you keep audit logs by default?
00:04:10 Samir Patel (Redwood SE): By default logs are retained 90 days, you can request longer retention for Dedicated with additional storage fees. We also support streaming logs to your SIEM via secure syslog or cloud logging connectors.
00:04:23 Laura Kim (Bluebridge Procurement): On the subprocessor list, we need to know any cloud infra partners and where backups live.
00:04:29 Maya Chen (Redwood AE): We'll share the current subprocessor list — at a high level it's standard cloud providers in the chosen region, and backups are retained per the DPA appendix with explicit region constraints for this account.
00:04:41 Marcus Liu (Bluebridge Finance): If we commit to a 12 month reserved pool what's the discount schedule and early termination terms?
00:04:48 Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Typical committed contracts have up to 30% discounts depending on GPU size and term; early termination is governed by the commercial schedule — for pilots we sometimes do a month-to-month with a 90-day notice to avoid lock-in, and then convert to reserved if desired.
00:05:02 Priya Shah (Bluebridge Legal): We also need right-to-audit language and breach notification windows — 72 hours is our minimum.
00:05:09 Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Redwood's standard is 72 hours for confirmed incidents; we can accept that in the DPA. We keep an incident response playbook and will share a redacted runbook for the pilot.
00:05:20 Anil Rao (Bluebridge InfoSec): For encryption in transit, are TLS certs customer-managed or Redwood-managed?
00:05:26 Samir Patel (Redwood SE): TLS is Redwood-managed by default, but you can supply certs for Dedicated/private setups; we support automated rotation or customer-managed certificate stores.
00:05:36 Laura Kim (Bluebridge Procurement): One procedural question: who's the legal contact on your side for redline negotiations so we can expedite?
00:05:42 Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Connect with me and Priya can loop her counsel; but Samir will be looped for technical clarifications. I'll introduce Julia Park (Redwood Legal) in the redline thread.
00:05:52 Marcus Liu (Bluebridge Finance): On invoicing and billing cycles, do you support net-45? We prefer net-45 for enterprise vendors.
00:05:58 Maya Chen (Redwood AE): We can do net-30 by default; net-45 is possible with enterprise contracts — I'll note finance as an approver and include options in the commercial schedule.
00:06:10 Priya Shah (Bluebridge Legal): Any compliance artifacts available? SOC 2, ISO, penetration test reports?
00:06:15 Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Yes, SOC 2 type 2 and periodic pen test executive summaries. We'll provide copies after an NDA; for pilot customers we often have a security package link.
00:06:26 Anil Rao (Bluebridge InfoSec): We'll need details on the pen test cadence and whether remediation windows are tracked.
00:06:30 Samir Patel (Redwood SE): Pen tests are annual and critical findings are tracked in our internal remediation tracker; we can provide a high-level remediation SLA for critical issues.
00:06:41 Laura Kim (Bluebridge Procurement): Okay, let's talk next steps. Marcus — finance needs committed spend number; what do you need from Redwood to model it?
00:06:50 Marcus Liu (Bluebridge Finance): A clear estimate of monthly committed tokens or reserved GPU hours, burst rates, and the committed discount schedule.
00:06:58 Maya Chen (Redwood AE): We'll send a pilot pricing spreadsheet with scenarios: low/medium/high usage, committed tokens or reserved vCPU/GPU hours, and overage rates. I'll aim to have that by 2027-04-19.
00:07:10 Priya Shah (Bluebridge Legal): We'll circulate redlines by 2027-04-20 if possible.
00:07:16 Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Great. I'll also share the DPA appendix with region pinning and the redwood security package link: https://redwood.docs/security/bluebridge-pkg
00:07:26 Anil Rao (Bluebridge InfoSec): Can we get a small benchmark run? Like a 2-hour test with a representative workload to see p95 latency under Dedicated small pool?
00:07:34 Samir Patel (Redwood SE): Yes — we can schedule a perf run. It requires a short setup window and some sample requests. I'll own that and propose times after we agree on the pilot SOW.
00:07:45 Laura Kim (Bluebridge Procurement): If we proceed, what's the contact for onboarding and entitlements?
00:07:50 Maya Chen (Redwood AE): The CSM will be assigned — for pilots it's usually a dedicated onboarding engineer plus my team for the commercial and legal path.
00:07:58 Marcus Liu (Bluebridge Finance): Fine — last question on export controls and data residency, do you have a clause for EU-only processing?
00:08:06 Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Yes, addendum available for EU-only processing. We'll flag that in the DPA and put the language in the redline draft.
00:08:14 Priya Shah (Bluebridge Legal): Okay let's recap next steps.
00:08:18 Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Recap: 1) Redwood to send redlined MSA/DPA template, security package, and pricing spreadsheet (target 2027-04-19/20). 2) Bluebridge to return redlines and procurement path by 2027-04-22. 3) Samir to schedule perf run and provide KV cache/prefix caching notes by 2027-04-19. 4) Align on pilot SOW and commit levels, then we aim to start pilot in early May.
00:09:02 Laura Kim (Bluebridge Procurement): That works. Anything else?
00:09:05 Marcus Liu (Bluebridge Finance): No, thanks everyone.
00:09:07 Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and a calendar invite for the perf run.

Notes / Links shared in call:
- Pricing spreadsheet link (redwood internal): https://redwood.app/sales/bluebridge-pricing (will be shared post-call)
- Security package: https://redwood.docs/security/bluebridge-pkg
- Pilot SOW template: https://redwood.docs/sow/pilot-template

End of transcript.
